headline: Discussed mouse cleanup at Public Access building, estimated at approximately $50,000; approved August minutes.
summary: Mouse activity was detected in the Public Access building, and a ServPro estimate for cleanup was approximately $50,000. Work will not start until the building is clear of rodents, and a pest management company is coming in to begin eradication. The group also discussed Channel 3 and Channel 85 programming and approved the August minutes.
decisions: Approved the August 3 meeting minutes; the vote was unanimous.

plain_text:
September 3, 2026 Cable TV Committee Meeting 
Present: Richard, Kathy, John, Lou, Jim, Pat, Barry, Danica, 1 Member of the Public 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order at 4:03 PM. 
 
2. Adjustments to the Agenda 
Richard would like to add a discussion about Council meeting audio quality to the agenda. 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
3.a August 3 Meeting Minutes 
 Motion by John, seconded by Kathy, to approve the August meeting minutes. 
Vote: Unanimous. 
 
4. New Business 
4.a. Welcome Barry Dodd, Public Access Director 
Committee members introduced themselves to Barry. Barry shared information 
about his background and experience with the Committee as well as his goals for 
the program. 
 
4.b. Public Access Building Update 
The Committee was presented information about the detected mouse activity that 
was discovered in the Public Accvess facility. Barry started cleaning in the facility 
and took down some ceiling tiles, discovering a significant amount of droppings 
between the tiles and insulation. This has been identified as the source of the 
lingering odor in the building. Staff brought ServPro in for an estimate of how much it 
would cost to remediate. Their proposal involves removing nearly all porous 
surfaces from the building for approximately $50,000. The Director of Code 
Enforcement has been consulted and completed a walkthrough of the building. The
Director is familiar with these situations and believes the necessary work can be 
done at a lower cost by a different company. He will be assisting Barry and Danica 
with a path forward that will likely include issuing a Request for Bids. Work at the 
facility should not begin until we are confident that the building is clear of rodents. A 
pest management company is coming in next week to begin the eradication 
process. 
Richard expressed concern about the political ramifications of asking the Council 
for this funding. He noted that the amount needed for cleanup is about the same 
amount that was requested for new equipment. 
Danica outlined potential ways to move forward, including asking to dip into the 20K 
difference between the FY27 program budget and FY27 estimated revenues. She 
assured the Committee that in all internal conversations, there has been no 
suggestion that anyone is interested in selling the building or relocating the 
program; all conversation has focused around how to move forward in that facility. 
Conversations with the Interim City Manager indicated that we could request that 
the Council funds remediation out of contingency. She has explained to the Interim 
City Manager the history of the misappropriation of franchise fee funds. 
Barry and Danica are meeting with SMPDC on Tuesday to talk about alternative 
sources of funding other than cable fees to support remediation of the building. 
Some members of the Committee expressed hesitation with seeking grant funding. 
Richard asked if he can come into the building to film. Out of an abundance of 
caution, the Code Enforcement Director said that the public should not enter the 
building, especially because the areas that are used to film are enclosed with low 
airflow. The committee discussed seeking a temporary space to film, such as at 
McArthur Library. 
 
4.c. Programming: Channel 3 vs. 85 
Government Access programming is currently on Channel 3 and Community TV is 
on Channel 85. Richard and Jim noted that this is a departure from past practice, 
where community programming was split between both channels. The idea was 
that people might come for the municipal programming and stay for community 
programs or vice versa. 
Channel 85 is viewable in Saco. We also have channels 1301 and 1302, and they 
play what is on 3 and 85, respectively.
Barry has set up a bulletin board on Channel 3 highlighting current events. 
Previously, meetings were playing at random times in a loop and getting cut off 
when we go live. Because there were no titles on the meeting, it would be unclear 
whether the meeting that a viewer was seeing was live or not. 
Jim would like to see the live meetings go on 85 because there is an on-demand way 
to watch city meetings already but there isn’t a way to watch community 
programming. Richard would be more comfortable with the split if the channels 
were adjacent and in lower numbers.  
Barry shared that the long-term goal is to have on-demand access to all 
programming that we do, and that he will cross-promote the content that is on each 
channel, so it would be easy for people to move between channels to find the 
content they want to see. He said he can talk to the Government Relations person 
with Spectrum about moving Channel 85 to a lower number, but these kinds of 
things will likely require reopening the franchise agreement. He has also talked to 
them about getting the channels into HD, but the process has changed since he 
accomplished that in Westbrook. 
Committee members confirmed that they were once cablecasting live out of the 
studio. 
 
5. Other Business 
John and Lou are not getting emails from Richard but got Danica’s emails. Danica 
believes this has to do with differences between City-issued and personal email 
accounts, and she will contact IT for support. 
John would like to discuss at a future meeting having Committee renamed to the 
Public Access Committee. 
 
6. Adjourn 
Motion by Kathy, seconded by Pat, to adjourn. 
Meeting adjourned at 5:37 p.m.
